quotes.text: The monorepo doesn't fail because of technical reasons. It fails because you've made coordination visible and then you pretended you could manage it with infrastructure instead of actually fixing the underlying organizational problem.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the episode's core thesis that monorepo failures are organizational, not technical.

quotes.text: The repository choice doesn't fix organizational fragmentation. It just changes how you see it. A fragmented organization will eventually break a monorepo.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Connects repository strategy to organizational structure in the spirit of Conway's law.

quotes.text: A monorepo does not reduce coordination overhead. It makes that overhead visible and concentrated. The problem doesn't go away. It just stops being invisible.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Debunks the central myth that a monorepo removes coordination costs.

quotes.text: If your organization is already struggling to coordinate, AI won't solve that. It amplifies it. It makes the bottleneck visible because that's where all the work is piling up.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why AI code generation exposes rather than fixes organizational fragmentation.

quotes.text: Consistency matters more than perfection. A suboptimal choice executed consistently beats a perfect choice executed halfway.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable, actionable principle for executing any repository strategy.

takeaways: Choosing a monorepo or multi-repo is really choosing where coordination happens: visibly in code review and CI, or invisibly in APIs, contracts and meetings.
Fragmentation comes from organizational debt such as unclear ownership, slow decision paths and inconsistent processes, and no repository strategy fixes it on its own.
Match your repository model to how your teams are actually coupled, measure coordination overhead and flow efficiency, and commit to the infrastructure or governance your choice requires.
hook: Many engineering leaders treat monorepo versus multi-repo as a Git question, yet their real problem is organizational fragmentation. This episode is for technical leaders and architects who want to understand why repository strategy mirrors team communication, how organizational debt and AI-generated code amplify coordination overhead, and how to choose a model that fits how their teams actually work.
